# 📊 Supl Plots: Data Preparation and Setup and initial visualiztion

```{r nmds_leke, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, results='hide', echo = FALSE}

nmdsLEKE <- metaMDS(zotu_df |>
                      filter(!str_detect(sample_id, "control")) |>
                      filter(!str_detect(sample_id, "CH|H")) |>
                      filter(!str_detect(sample_id, "KT1")) |>
                      filter(!str_detect(sample_id, "KA5")) |>
                      filter(str_detect(sample_id, "O_|K_|G_")) |>
                      column_to_rownames("sample_id"), 
                        distance = "bray", k = 2, trymax = 9999)


NMDSscoreLEKE <- scores(nmdsLEKE , display = "sites") %>% 
  as.data.frame() %>% 
  rownames_to_column("sample_id") %>% 
  left_join(meta_data, by = "sample_id")
# Save NMDS scores table (optional)
# write.csv(NMDSscoreLEKE, "output/NMDS_scores_leke.csv", row.names = FALSE)

NMDSstressLEKE <- round(nmdsLEKE$stress,2) * 100



NMDSscoreLEKE_new <- NMDSscoreLEKE |>
  mutate(
    label = paste0(commonname, "\n", sample_site),
    commonname_color = case_when(
      commonname == "ʻōhiʻa Lehua" ~ "ʻōhiʻa Lehua",
      commonname == "koa" ~ "koa",
      commonname == "strawberry guava" ~ "strawberry guava",
      TRUE ~ "other"
    ),
    elev_arrow = case_when(
      elevation == "high" ~ "\u25B2",
      elevation == "mid"  ~ "\u25A0",
      elevation == "low"  ~ "\u25BC"
    )
  )

# Set your color palette
plant_colors <- c("ʻōhiʻa Lehua" = "#C1133D",
      "koa" = "#8B4513",
      "strawberry guava" = "gold")

hull_data_tree_leke <- 
  NMDSscoreLEKE_new %>%
   mutate(label = paste0(commonname, "\n", sample_site)) |>
  group_by(label) %>% 
  dplyr::slice(chull(NMDS1, NMDS2))

#we want to visualize the two different ridges and want to see their dissimiliarty

nmds_tree_plot_leke <- NMDSscoreLEKE_new |>
  ggplot() +

  geom_text(
    aes(NMDS1, NMDS2, label = elev_arrow, color = commonname_color),
    size = 6, show.legend = FALSE
  ) +

  geom_point(
    data = NMDSscoreLEKE_new |> 
      distinct(label, elevation, shortname, commonname_color),
    aes(x = 999, y = 999, fill = commonname_color, shape = elevation),
    color = "black",
    size = 4,
    show.legend = TRUE,
    inherit.aes = FALSE
  ) +

  geom_polygon(
    data = hull_data_tree_leke,
    aes(NMDS1, NMDS2, fill = commonname_color, color = commonname_color, group = label),
    alpha = 0.2
  ) +

  scale_color_manual(values = plant_colors) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = plant_colors) +
  scale_shape_manual(
    name = "Elevation",
    values = c("high" = 24, "mid" = 22, "low" = 25)
  ) +
  coord_cartesian(xlim = c(-.2,.2), ylim = c(-.2,.2)) +
  labs(x = glue("MDS1 \nStress = {NMDSstressLEKE} %"),
       y = "MDS2",
       fill = "Tree species",
       color = "Tree species") +
  theme_classic() +
  theme(
    legend.title = element_text(size = 13),
    legend.text = element_text(size = 13),
    axis.text = element_markdown(size = 13, color = "black"),
    axis.title = element_text(color = "black")
  )

  
nmdsohia <- metaMDS(zotu_df |>
                      filter(!str_detect(sample_id, "control")) |>
                      filter(!str_detect(sample_id, "CH|H")) |>
                      filter(!str_detect(sample_id, "KT1")) |>

                      filter(!str_detect(sample_id, "K_|G_")) |>
                      column_to_rownames("sample_id"), 
                        distance = "bray", k = 2, trymax = 9999)

NMDSscoresohia <- scores(nmdsohia , display = "sites") %>%

# Save NMDS scores table (optional)

NMDSstressohia <- round(nmdsohia$stress,2) * 100


hull_data_site <- 
  NMDSscoresohia %>%
  drop_na(sample_site) %>%

  dplyr::slice(chull(NMDS1, NMDS2))

hull_data_elevation <- 
  NMDSscoresohia %>%
  group_by(elevation) %>% 
  dplyr::slice(chull(NMDS1, NMDS2))

hull_data_tree <- 
  NMDSscoresohia %>%
  group_by(commonname) %>% 
  dplyr::slice(chull(NMDS1, NMDS2))
nmds_site_plot <-  NMDSscoresohia |> 
  mutate(elev_arrow = case_when(
    elevation == "high" ~ "\u25B2",  # ▲
    elevation == "mid"  ~ "\u25A0",  # ■
    elevation == "low"  ~ "\u25BC"   # ▼
  )) |> 
  ggplot() +
  
  # main glyph layer
  geom_text(
    aes(NMDS1, NMDS2, label = elev_arrow, color = sample_site),

  geom_point(
    data = NMDSscoresohia |> distinct(sample_site, elevation),
    aes(x = 999, y = 999, fill = sample_site, shape = elevation),
    color = "black",

    show.legend = TRUE,

  ) +
  
  # group hulls

    data = hull_data_site,
    aes(NMDS1, NMDS2, color = sample_site, fill = sample_site),

  ) +

  scale_color_npg() +
  scale_fill_npg() +
  coord_cartesian(xlim = c(-.5,.5), ylim = c(-.5,.5)) +
  scale_shape_manual(
    name = "Elevation",
    values = c("high" = 24, "mid" = 22, "low" = 25)
  ) +
  
  labs(x = glue("MDS1 \nStress = {NMDSstressohia} %"),
       y = "MDS2",
       fill = "Ridges on Oahu",
       color = "Ridges on Oahu") +
  
  theme_classic() +
  theme(
    legend.title = element_text(size = 13),
    legend.text = element_text(size = 13),
    axis.text = element_markdown(size = 13, color = "black"),
    axis.title = element_text(color = "black")
  )


nmds_elevation_plot <-  NMDSscoresohia |> 
  mutate(elev_arrow = case_when(
    elevation == "high" ~ "\u25B2",  # ▲
    elevation == "mid"  ~ "\u25A0",  # ■
    elevation == "low"  ~ "\u25BC"   # ▼
  )) |> 
  ggplot() +
  
  # arrow symbols
  geom_text(
    aes(NMDS1, NMDS2, label = elev_arrow, color = elevation),
    size = 6, show.legend = FALSE
  ) +
  
  # dummy layer to build legend
  geom_point(
    data = NMDSscoresohia |> distinct(elevation, commonname),
    aes(x = 999, y = 999, fill = elevation, shape = commonname),
    color = "black",

  geom_polygon(
    data = hull_data_elevation,
    aes(NMDS1, NMDS2, color = elevation, fill = elevation),

  ) +

  scale_shape_manual(

  theme_classic() +

    legend.text = element_text(size = 13),
    axis.text = element_markdown(size = 13, color = "black"),

  )



nmds_ohia_plot <-  NMDSscoresohia |> 
  mutate(elev_arrow = case_when(

    elevation == "low"  ~ "\u25BC"   # ▼

  # plot the Unicode arrows
  geom_text(

   geom_point(
```

# 📊 Plot 2: NMDS panel
```{r nmds-panel, echo=FALSE, fig.width=8, fig.height=12, out.width="100%", fig.align="center", warning = FALSE}
#save this to png and svg file with dynamic date with paste0

ggsave(here::here("figures", paste0("NMDS_panel_", Sys.Date(), ".png")), 
       plot = NMDS_panel, 
       width = 8, height = 12, dpi = 300)
NMDS_panel
```

Figure X: Arthropod assemblages differ more strongly by site than elevation: Two-dimensional NMDS plots based on presence-absence data of arthropod communities from eDNA samples show that sampling site explains more variation in community composition than elevation.Top panel Comparison of the three most common trees across a small elevation gradient on Aiea & Manana Ridge. Stress value above 20% Middle panel: The same NMDS ordination, now grouped by sampling site; colored polygons highlight that samples from the same site cluster tightly despite differing in elevation. Each shape indicates the elevation level of the sample (triangles = high, inverted triangles = low, squares = mid). Stress value of 15% indicates a reliable two-dimensional representation of dissimilarities. Bottom panel: Samples grouped by elevation level (high, mid, low) across all sites; shaded polygons connect samples from the same elevation.

# Statistical Analyses mainly focusing on ß-diversity

## Section 1: Insect-Community differences by Trees (Manana and Aiea Ridge)

```{r statistical-setup-leke, warning = FALSE, echo = FALSE}
# Prepare matrix and metadata for PERMANOVA
zotu_leke <- zotu_df |> 
  filter(!str_detect(sample_id, "control")) |> 
  filter(!str_detect(sample_id, "CH|H")) |> 
  filter(!str_detect(sample_id, "KT1|KA5")) |> 
  filter(str_detect(sample_id, "O_|K_|G_")) |> 
  column_to_rownames("sample_id")

```

```{r statistical-tests-leke, echo = FALSE, warning = FALSE}
# Calculate Bray-Curtis dissimilarity between samples
bray_leke <- vegdist(zotu_leke, method = "bray")
# Prepare Prepare matching metadata for only the samples used
meta_leke <- meta_data |> filter(sample_id %in% rownames(zotu_leke))

# Run PERMANOVA to test if tree type significantly affects community composition
adonis_leke <- adonis2(bray_leke ~ commonname, data = meta_leke)
print(adonis_leke)
# Save PERMANOVA results (optional)
# capture.output(adonis_leke, file = "output/permanova_leke.txt")

```

While the PERMANOVA test did not find significant differences in community composition between tree species (p = 0.895), the NMDS ordination suggests that samples from ʻōhiʻa, koa, and strawberry guava form visually distinct clusters. This pattern may indicate subtle differences in arthropod communities that are not statistically detectable at the current sample size. Also r squared value is very low, indicating that tree type does not explain much of the variation in community composition.

## 📊 Supl Plot: Beta-dispersion Test: Tree Type Group Variability

```{r beta-disp-leke ,echo = FALSE}
disp_leke <- betadisper(bray_leke, meta_leke$commonname)
permutest(disp_leke)
# Save beta-dispersion test output (optional)
# capture.output(permutest(disp_leke), file = "output/betadispersion_leke.txt")
```

There is no significant difference in dispersion (beta diversity spread) among tree species (p = 0.588). This suggests the PERMANOVA assumption of equal group dispersions is not violated, which is good.

## Section 2: ʻŌhiʻa – Community differences by Site

```{r statistical-setup2, warning = FALSE, echo = FALSE}
# Ensure sample_id is character
meta_data$sample_id <- as.character(meta_data$sample_id)
zotu_df$sample_id <- as.character(zotu_df$sample_id)

# Merge metadata with zotu table, remove controls
merged_df <- meta_data %>% 
  inner_join(zotu_df, by = "sample_id") |> 
  filter(!str_detect(sample_id, "control"))

# Extract OTU matrix for analysis
zotu_matrix <- merged_df %>% 
  select(starts_with("zotu")) %>% 
  as.matrix()
rownames(zotu_matrix) <- merged_df$sample_id

# Calculate Bray-Curtis dissimilarity
bray_dist <- vegdist(zotu_matrix, method = "bray")
```

```{r ohia-site-statistics, echo = FALSE}
# --------------------------------------------
# 1. OHIA ONLY - Differences between sites
ohia_df <- merged_df %>% filter(commonname == "ʻōhiʻa Lehua")
zotu_ohia <- ohia_df %>% select(starts_with("zotu")) %>% as.matrix()
rownames(zotu_ohia) <- ohia_df$sample_id
bray_ohia <- vegdist(zotu_ohia, method = "bray")

# PERMANOVA for sample_site within Ohia
adonis_ohia_site <- adonis2(bray_ohia ~ sample_site, data = ohia_df)
print(adonis_ohia_site)
```

A PERMANOVA based on Bray-Curtis dissimilarities showed that arthropod community composition within ʻōhiʻa stands varied significantly by sampling site (R² = 0.21, p = 0.002), suggesting strong site-specific effects across the Oʻahu gradient.

## 📊 Supl Plot: Beta Diversity Decomposition

```{r ohia-betadisp-plot-setup, echo = FALSE}

ohia_dispersion <- betadisper(bray_ohia, ohia_df$sample_site)
ohia_df_disp <- data.frame(distance = ohia_dispersion$distances,
                            tree_species = ohia_df$commonname,
                           sample_site = ohia_df$sample_site,
                           island = ohia_df$island)
ohia_df_disp |>
  filter(island != "Hawaii") |> 
  ggplot(aes(x = sample_site, y = distance, fill = sample_site)) +
  geom_boxplot() +
  scale_fill_npg() +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(
    title = "Beta Dispersion across ʻōhiʻa sites on Oʻahu",
    x = "Sample Site",
    y = "Distance to Centroid",
    fill = "Ridges"
  )


permutest(ohia_dispersion)

```

Although community dispersion varied visually across sampling sites, a test for homogeneity of multivariate dispersions was not statistically significant (F = 1.87, p = 0.119). This supports the validity of the PERMANOVA result, indicating that observed differences in arthropod community composition across ʻōhiʻa sites are not driven by differences in within-site variability.

## Section 3: ʻŌhiʻa – Community differences by elevation

```{r ohia-elevations-statistics, echo = FALSE}
# --------------------------------------------
# 2. OHIA ONLY - Differences by elevation

elev_dispersion <- betadisper(bray_ohia, ohia_df$commonname)
elev_df_disp <- data.frame(distance = ohia_dispersion$distances,
                            tree_species = ohia_df$commonname,
                           sample_site = ohia_df$sample_site,
                           island = ohia_df$island,
                           elevation = ohia_df$elevation)

# Create plotting df
elev_df_disp <- data.frame(
  distance = elev_dispersion$distances,
  elevation = ohia_df$elevation,
  sample_site = ohia_df$sample_site,
  island = ohia_df$island
)

# Boxplot showing within-group beta dispersion by elevation
elev_df_disp |>
  filter(island != "Hawaii") |>
  ggplot(aes(x = elevation, y = distance, fill = elevation)) +
  geom_boxplot() +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(
    title = "Beta Dispersion across elevation groups (ʻŌhiʻa only)",
    x = "Elevation", y = "Distance to Centroid"
  )
```

```{r elevations-statistics, echo = FALSE}
adonis_ohia_elev <- adonis2(bray_ohia ~ elevation, data = ohia_df)
print(adonis_ohia_elev)

elev_dispersion <- betadisper(bray_ohia, ohia_df$elevation)  # ✅ fix
permutest(elev_dispersion)  # (optional but important)
```

We found no significant differences in arthropod community composition across elevations within ʻōhiʻa stands (PERMANOVA: R² = 0.058, p = 0.401). However, a test for homogeneity of dispersions revealed that beta diversity varied significantly across elevations (F = 5.18, p = 0.013), indicating that community consistency differs with elevation despite no shift in centroids.

```{r permanova-combined, warning - FALSE, echo = FALSE}
# Subset only ʻōhiʻa samples from Oʻahu
ohia_oahu_df <- merged_df %>%
  filter(commonname == "ʻōhiʻa Lehua", island == "Oahu")

# Prepare OTU matrix and Bray-Curtis distance
zotu_ohia_oahu <- ohia_oahu_df %>%
  select(starts_with("zotu")) %>%
  as.matrix()
rownames(zotu_ohia_oahu) <- ohia_oahu_df$sample_id

bray_ohia_oahu <- vegdist(zotu_ohia_oahu, method = "bray")

# Run combined PERMANOVA
adonis_ohia_combined <- adonis2(
  bray_ohia_oahu ~ sample_site + elevation,
  data = ohia_oahu_df
)

print(adonis_ohia_combined)
```

A combined PERMANOVA model revealed that site and elevation together significantly structured arthropod community composition within ʻōhiʻa stands across Oʻahu (R² = 0.34, p = 0.001). These variables jointly explained \~34% of the observed variation, indicating that spatial and elevational differences play a strong role in shaping arthropod assemblages within this native forest type.

# Beta-diversity within between subsets

```{r beta-within-between, echo = FALSE, fig.width=8, fig.height=12, out.width="100%", fig.align="center", warning = FALSE}
#create a df from ohia distance matrix

meta_data_short1 <- meta_data %>% 
  select(sample_id, sample_site, elevation, island, commonname) |> 
  rename_with(~ paste0(., "_1"), -sample_id)

meta_data_short2 <- meta_data %>% 
  select(sample_id, sample_site, elevation, island,commonname) |> 
  rename_with(~ paste0(., "_2"), -sample_id)

bray_ohia_df <- as.matrix(bray_ohia) |> 
  as.data.frame() |> 
  rownames_to_column(var = "sample_id") |>
  pivot_longer(-sample_id, names_to = "sample_id2", values_to = "distance") |>
  left_join(meta_data_short1, by = c("sample_id" = "sample_id"), suffix = c("", "_s1")) |>
  filter(sample_id != sample_id2) |>
  left_join(meta_data_short2, by = c("sample_id2" = "sample_id"), c("", "_s2")) 

bray_leke <- as.matrix(bray_dist) |> 
  as.data.frame() |> 
  rownames_to_column(var = "sample_id") |>
  pivot_longer(-sample_id, names_to = "sample_id2", values_to = "distance") |>
  left_join(meta_data_short1, by = c("sample_id" = "sample_id"), suffix = c("", "_s1")) |>
  filter(sample_id != sample_id2) |>
  left_join(meta_data_short2, by = c("sample_id2" = "sample_id"), c("", "_s2")) 

within_sites <- bray_ohia_df |>
  filter(sample_site_1 == sample_site_2) |> 
  filter(island_1 == "Oahu") |> 
  filter(island_2 == "Oahu") |> 
  mutate(comparison = "within sites",
         order = "1_all_sites")

between_sites <- bray_ohia_df |>
  filter(sample_site_1 != sample_site_2) |> 
  filter(sample_site_1 < sample_site_2) |> 
   filter(island_1 == "Oahu") |> 
  filter(island_2 == "Oahu") |> 
  mutate(comparison = "between sites",
         order = "1_all_sites")

within_elevation <- bray_ohia_df |>
  filter(elevation_1 == elevation_2) |> 
  filter(island_1 == "Oahu", island_2 == "Oahu") |> 
  mutate(comparison = "within elevation", 
         order = "2_elevation_category")

between_elevation <- bray_ohia_df |>
  filter(elevation_1 != elevation_2) |> 
  filter(sample_site_1 < sample_site_2) |> 
  filter(island_1 == "Oahu") |> 
  filter(island_2 == "Oahu") |>  
  mutate(comparison = "between elevation",
         order = "2_elevation_category")

within_elevation_leke <- bray_leke |>
  filter(elevation_1 == elevation_1) |> 
  filter(str_detect(sample_site_1, "Manana|Aiea")) |> 
  filter(str_detect(sample_site_2, "Manana|Aiea")) |> 
  mutate(comparison = "within elevation Leke",
         order = "3_elevation_leke")

between_elevation_leke <- bray_leke |>
  filter(elevation_1 != elevation_2) |> 
  filter(str_detect(sample_site_1, "Manana|Aiea")) |> 
  filter(str_detect(sample_site_2, "Manana|Aiea")) |> 
  filter(sample_site_1 < sample_site_2) |> 
  mutate(comparison = "between elevation Leke",
         order = "3_elevation_leke")

within_trees_leke <- bray_leke |>
  filter(commonname_1 == commonname_2) |> 
  filter(str_detect(sample_site_1, "Manana|Aiea")) |> 
  filter(str_detect(sample_site_2, "Manana|Aiea")) |> 
  mutate(comparison = "within tree species Leke",
         order = "4_different_trees")

between_trees_leke <- bray_leke |>
  filter(commonname_1 != commonname_2) |> 
  filter(str_detect(sample_site_1, "Manana|Aiea")) |> 
  filter(str_detect(sample_site_2, "Manana|Aiea")) |> 
  filter(sample_site_1 < sample_site_2) |> 
  mutate(comparison = "between tree species Leke",
         order = "4_different_trees")


beta_comp <- bind_rows(
  within_sites, between_sites, 
  within_elevation, between_elevation,
  between_elevation_leke,within_elevation_leke,
  within_trees_leke, between_trees_leke)

beta_comb_plot <- beta_comp |>
  mutate(comparison = as.factor(comparison))|>
  ggplot(aes(x = fct_reorder(comparison, order), 
             y = distance)) +
  geom_boxplot() +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(title = "Beta Diversity across all ‘Ōhi‘a samples from O‘ahu\nGrouped by comparison type",
       x = "Comparison", 
       y = "beta diversity distance") +
  facet_wrap(~order, scales = "free_x", ncol =1) +
  theme_classic() +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))

ggsave(here::here("figures/beta_diversity_comparison.png"),
       plot =beta_comb_plot,
       width = 10, 
       height = 10, 
       units = "in")


beta_comb_plot
```

```{r beta-within-between-statistics, echo = FALSE, warning = FALSE}
# Kruskal-Wallis test across all groups
kruskal_result <- kruskal.test(distance ~ comparison, data = beta_comp)
print(kruskal_result)

# Pairwise Wilcoxon tests with FDR correction
pairwise_result <- pairwise.wilcox.test(beta_comp$distance,
                                        beta_comp$comparison,
                                        p.adjust.method = "fdr")
print(pairwise_result)
```

Pairwise Wilcoxon tests comparing Bray-Curtis dissimilarities revealed significantly greater beta diversity between elevations, tree species, and sites than within these groups (FDR-corrected p \< 0.001 for most contrasts). Notably, arthropod communities differed significantly between tree species where all three co-occurred, and between elevation bands both within and across sites. Within-site and within-elevation comparisons consistently showed lower dissimilarity, indicating stronger community cohesion at those scales.

# Beta Diversity Decomposition based on Sorensen Family

We want to expose the components of beta diversity, specifically turnover and nestedness, using the Sorensen index. This will help us understand how much of the dissimilarity is due to species turnover versus nestedness.

-Are differences between communities driven by species replacement (turnover)?

-Or by nestedness (e.g. lowland sites losing taxa)?

-Which sites are more compositionally heterogeneous (high within-site turnover)?

This goes beyond Bray-Curtis, offering more ecological insight.

```{r decomposition-setup, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, results='hide', echo = FALSE}

#Beta Diversity Decomposition
# Convert to presence/absence to bee 100% sure
zotu_pa <- zotu_df |>
  filter(!str_detect(sample_id, "control")) |>
  filter(!str_detect(sample_id, "CH|H")) |>
  filter(!str_detect(sample_id, "KT1|KA5")) |>
  filter(!str_detect(sample_id, "G_|K_")) |>
  column_to_rownames("sample_id") |> 
  mutate(across(everything(), ~ if_else(.x > 0, 1, 0))) |> 
  as.matrix()

#str(zotu_pa)

# Compute beta diversity components
beta_part <- beta.pair(zotu_pa, index.family = "sorensen")
#str(beta_part)

# This gives:
# - beta_part$beta.sor: total dissimilarity
# - beta_part$beta.sim: turnover
# - beta_part$beta.sne: nestedness-resultant
```

NMDS based on beta.sim will show us the turnover component of beta diversity, which is the species replacement component. This will help us understand how much of the dissimilarity is due to species turnover versus nestedness.

```{r decomposition-plot, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, results='hide', echo = FALSE}

# Example: NMDS on turnover
nmds_ohia_turn <- metaMDS(beta_part$beta.sim, k = 2, trymax = 9999)

# Extract site scores and merge with metadata
NMDSscores_ohia_turn <- scores(nmds_ohia_turn, display = "sites") |>
  as.data.frame() |>
  rownames_to_column("sample_id") |>
  left_join(meta_data, by = "sample_id")

# Extract stress value (as %)
NMDSstress_ohia_turn <- round(nmds_ohia_turn$stress, 2) * 100

# Stress plot
stressplot(nmds_ohia_turn)

hull_ohia_turn <- 
  NMDSscores_ohia_turn %>%
  drop_na(sample_site) %>%
  group_by(sample_site) %>% 
  dplyr::slice(chull(NMDS1, NMDS2))

nmds_ohia_turn_plot <-  NMDSscores_ohia_turn |> 
  mutate(elev_arrow = case_when(
    elevation == "high" ~ "\u25B2",  # ▲
    elevation == "mid"  ~ "\u25A0",  # ■
    elevation == "low"  ~ "\u25BC"   # ▼
  )) |> 
  ggplot() +
  
  # main glyph layer
  geom_text(
    aes(NMDS1, NMDS2, label = elev_arrow, color = sample_site),
    size = 6, show.legend = FALSE
  ) +
  
  # dummy for combined shape + color legend
  geom_point(
    data = NMDSscores_ohia_turn |> distinct(sample_site, elevation),
    aes(x = 999, y = 999, fill = sample_site, shape = elevation),
    color = "black",
    size = 4,
    show.legend = TRUE,
    inherit.aes = FALSE
  ) +
  
  # group hulls
  geom_polygon(
    data = hull_ohia_turn,
    aes(NMDS1, NMDS2, color = sample_site, fill = sample_site),
    alpha = 0.2
  ) +

  scale_color_npg() +
  scale_fill_npg() +
  coord_cartesian(xlim = c(-1,1), ylim = c(-1,1)) +
  scale_shape_manual(
    name = "Elevation",
    values = c("high" = 24, "mid" = 22, "low" = 25)
  ) +
  
  labs(x = glue("MDS1 \nStress = {NMDSstress_ohia_turn} %"),
       y = "MDS2") +
  
  theme_classic() +
  theme(
    legend.title = element_text(size = 13),
    legend.text = element_text(size = 13),
    axis.text = element_markdown(size = 13, color = "black"),
    axis.title = element_text(color = "black")
  )


nmds_ohia_turn_plot

```

```{r pro-test, echo = FALSE, warning = FALSE}
pro <- protest(nmdsohia, nmds_ohia_turn)
summary(pro)
```

MDS ordinations based on Bray–Curtis and Sørensen turnover dissimilarities both revealed strong ridge-level structuring of arthropod communities. While the Bray–Curtis NMDS (Stress = 15%) yielded a slightly better fit than the Sørensen-based NMDS (Stress = 17%), both metrics showed consistent clustering. The Sørensen ordination emphasizes species turnover alone, confirming that site-level differences are driven not only by shifts in abundance but also by distinct species pools. The Bray–Curtis plot further suggests that relative abundance patterns reinforce community structure, particularly within elevation bands.

A Procrustes analysis comparing the Bray–Curtis and Sørensen turnover NMDS ordinations revealed a high degree of congruence (Procrustes sum of squares = 0.208, RMSE = 0.102), with minimal rotation or scaling required. This confirms that site-level community differences are primarily driven by species turnover, and that patterns are consistent across presence–absence and abundance-based metrics

```{r decomposition-stats, echo = FALSE, warning = FALSE}

# Turnover matrix to average per site
turn_mat <- as.matrix(beta_part$beta.sim)

ohia_meta <- meta_data |>
  filter(!str_detect(sample_id, "control")) |>
  filter(!str_detect(sample_id, "CH|H")) |>
  filter(!str_detect(sample_id, "KT1|KA5")) |>
  filter(!str_detect(sample_id, "G_|K_")) |>
  arrange(base::match(sample_id, rownames(turn_mat)))

# Sanity check
stopifnot(all(ohia_meta$sample_id == rownames(turn_mat)))

# Calculate average pairwise turnover *within* each site
site_turnover <- ohia_meta |>
  select(sample_id, sample_site) |>
  group_by(sample_site) |>
  summarise(mean_turnover = {
    # Get sample IDs for this site
    ids <- sample_id
    # Subset the matrix
    site_dist <- turn_mat[ids, ids, drop = FALSE]
    
    # Extract lower triangle (pairwise distances, no double-counting)
    lower_vals <- site_dist[lower.tri(site_dist)]
    
    # Mean of those values (NA if only 1 sample)
    if (length(lower_vals) >= 1) mean(lower_vals) else NA_real_
  })

site_turnover
```

```{r decomposition-stats2, echo = FALSE, warning = FALSE}
adonis_turn <- adonis2(beta_part$beta.sim ~ sample_site + elevation, data = ohia_meta)
print(adonis_turn)

turn_disp <- betadisper(beta_part$beta.sim, group = ohia_meta$sample_site)
permutest(turn_disp)

kruskal.test(mean_turnover ~ sample_site, data = site_turnover)

pairwise.wilcox.test(site_turnover$mean_turnover, site_turnover$sample_site, p.adjust.method = "fdr")

```

Decomposition of beta diversity showed that community dissimilarity among ʻōhiʻa stands was primarily driven by species turnover, rather than nestedness. A PERMANOVA based on turnover distances revealed significant effects of site and elevation (R² = 0.38, p = 0.001), while a dispersion test confirmed homogeneity of within-group variance (p = 0.679). Mean within-site turnover ranged from 0.68 to 0.81, with no significant differences among sites (Kruskal–Wallis p = 0.406), indicating consistently high compositional variability across the landscape.

# Geospatial Distance Decay and Mantel Test

```{r geospatial-distance-decay, echo = FALSE, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE}
# Geospatial Distance Decay and Mantel Test
# --------------------------------------------

# 1. Filter metadata and ZOTU table to match Bray-Curtis community matrix
ohia_meta <- meta_data |>
  filter(!str_detect(sample_id, "control|CH|H|KT1")) |>
  arrange(base::match(sample_id, zotu_df$sample_id))

# 2. Filter ZOTU matrix accordingly
zotu_df <- zotu_df |> column_to_rownames("sample_id")
ohia_meta <- ohia_meta |> mutate(sample_id = as.character(sample_id))
zotu_ids <- rownames(zotu_df)
# base::intersect(ohia_meta$sample_id, zotu_ids)
# base::setdiff(ohia_meta$sample_id, zotu_ids)
zotu_filtered <- zotu_df[ohia_meta$sample_id, ]

# 3. Calculate Bray-Curtis dissimilarity

bray_dist <- vegdist(zotu_filtered, method = "bray")

# 4. Compute geographic distances using longitude and latitude (Haversine in meters)
library(geosphere)
geo_coords <- ohia_meta |> 
  select(longitude= coord_y, latitude = coord_x) |> 
  drop_na(latitude) |>
  drop_na(longitude)  |> 
  as.matrix()

geo_dist <- distm(geo_coords, fun = distHaversine)
rownames(geo_dist) <- ohia_meta$sample_id
colnames(geo_dist) <- ohia_meta$sample_id

# 5. Extract lower triangle for plotting distance decay
geo_vals <- geo_dist[lower.tri(geo_dist)]
bray_vals <- as.matrix(bray_dist)[lower.tri(as.matrix(bray_dist))]

# 6. Fit and summarize linear model
decay_model <- lm(bray_vals ~ geo_vals)
summary(decay_model)

```

Community dissimilarity increased significantly with geographic distance (R² = 0.081, p \< 0.0001). While the effect size is modest, this supports a weak but significant distance-decay pattern of arthropod communities across ridges and elevations. Even across small spatial scales, localized turnover contributes to beta diversity.

```{r, manteltest, echo = FALSE, warning = FALSE}
#compare geographical distance to bray curtis dissimilarity

mantel_result <- mantel(as.dist(geo_dist), bray_dist, method = "pearson", permutations = 9999)
print(mantel_result)

```

# 📊 Supl Plot: Mantel-test and Distance Decay Plot
```{r distance-decay-plot, echo = FALSE, warning = FALSE}

# 7. create plot 
# 7.1 Extract lower triangle
bray_vals <- as.matrix(bray_dist)[lower.tri(bray_dist)]
geo_vals <- geo_dist[lower.tri(geo_dist)]

# 7.2 Create a data frame for plotting
dist_decay_df <- data.frame(
  geo = geo_vals,
  bray = bray_vals
)

# 7.3 Fit linear model
decay_model <- lm(bray ~ geo, data = dist_decay_df)
lm_r2 <- summary(decay_model)$r.squared

# 7.4 Run Mantel test
mantel_result <- vegan::mantel(as.dist(geo_dist), bray_dist, permutations = 9999, method = "pearson")

# 7.5 actual Plot
ggplot(dist_decay_df, aes(x = geo, y = bray)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.5, size = 1.5) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", color = "red", se = FALSE) +
  annotate("text", x = max(dist_decay_df$geo) * 0.8, y = .5,
           label = paste0("Mantel r = ", round(mantel_result$statistic, 3),
                          "\np = ", format.pval(mantel_result$signif, digits = 3),
                          "\nR² = ", round(lm_r2, 2)),
           hjust = 0, vjust = 1, size = 4,
           fontface = "italic", color = "black") +
  labs(
    title = "Distance Decay of Community Similarity",
    x = "Geographic distance (meters)",
    y = "Bray-Curtis dissimilarity"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()


# Save in subfolder "figues"
ggsave(
  filename = here::here("figures", paste0("distance_decay_", Sys.Date(), ".png")),
  plot = last_plot(),
  width = 7,
  height = 5,
  dpi = 300
)
```

A Mantel test revealed a significant correlation between Bray-Curtis dissimilarity and geographic distance (r = 0.284, p = 0.0001), indicating a moderate but statistically robust distance-decay pattern in arthropod community composition across sampling sites.

This suggests that geographic separation contributes to community turnover, even after accounting for local habitat effects. The result aligns with the idea that dispersal limitation or historical biogeography plays a role in shaping beta diversity along Hawaiian forest gradients.

# Summary initial analyses

This report demonstrates that arthropod communities across Hawaiian forest gradients are shaped by a combination of spatial structure, elevational zonation, and forest composition. Using eDNA-based metabarcoding and a suite of multivariate analyses, we find:

Community composition in ʻōhiʻa forests varies significantly across sites (PERMANOVA R² = 0.21, p = 0.002) and is further influenced by elevation (combined R² = 0.34, p = 0.001).

Tree species identity, when tested in co-occurring sites (e.g., Manana and ʻAiea), does not explain significant variation in community structure (p = 0.895), though NMDS ordinations suggest subtle clustering.

Beta diversity decomposition reveals that community differences are primarily driven by species turnover rather than nestedness, with turnover significantly structured by site and elevation (R² = 0.38, p = 0.001).

Beta-dispersion patterns support consistent within-site heterogeneity and do not confound PERMANOVA results.

Distance–decay patterns indicate a weak but significant effect of geographic distance on community dissimilarity (Mantel r = 0.284, p = 0.0001), suggesting that even over short distances, dispersal limitation or spatial structuring contributes to beta diversity.

Together, these findings highlight the strong role of site-specific conditions and elevation in structuring arthropod communities in Hawaiian forests, while tree species identity plays a secondary role. The integration of turnover-based decomposition and spatial statistics adds ecological depth and supports the use of eDNA as a scalable tool for arthropod biodiversity monitoring across complex landscapes.
